Balanced-hawkish hold: The FOMC maintained the federal funds rate at 5.25–5.50% and continued balance-sheet runoff of Treasuries and agency MBS. This stance is consistent with Taylor-rule guidance when inflation is above the 2% objective and activity is strong, while the statement’s emphasis on “cumulative tightening” and “lags” aligns with the literature on transmission through credit and bank-lending channels (e.g., Bernanke–Gertler–Gilchrist). Implementation via IOER at 5.4%, ON RRP, and standing repo facilities reflects the post-2008 floor system, and the focus on inflation expectations and wage–price dynamics mirrors short-run Phillips curve considerations. QT likely tightens via reserves and term-premium effects, consistent with work on balance-sheet policies and the yield curve (e.g., Cochrane–Piazzesi). Net tone: modestly positive on growth and banking resilience, but constrained by elevated inflation risks and restrictive policy settings.
